Emily earned $800 at her part-time job last semester. This semester, she received a 15% increase in her salary. How much money will she make in total for the two semesters?
Emily designs a 15-story skyscraper. The first 8 stories are each 15 feet tall, while the remaining floors are each 2 feet taller. How tall is the skyscraper?

Alicia is in charge of collecting donations from a charity box at the local museum. During the morning hour, she collected 20 donations. Over the next three hours, she collected 40 donations each hour. In the fifth hour, she collected 60 donations, but she had to give 10 of them to her supervisor to cover an administrative fee. How many donations did Alicia have after the fifth hour?

Emily is planning to make 200 scarves for a charity event. She has already completed 20 scarves, and today, she finished twice as many scarves. How many scarves should she make tomorrow if she wants to complete one-third of the remaining number of scarves needed?

Emily is traveling to the beach at a speed of 75 mph. The distance to the beach is 450 miles. She plans to stop for lunch and rest for 2 hours along the way. How long will it take her to reach the beach?

Josiah puts a quarter in his piggy bank every day for 24 days.  Leah saves 50 cents in an empty pickle jar every day for 20 days. Megan saves twice as much as Leah for 12 days.   How much do the three children save together?
There are 50 staplers in the stapler.  Stacie staples 3 dozen reports on her desk.  How many staplers are left in the stapler?

Emily is employed by a firm that offers a vacation package: for every 12 days worked, she earns 1 day off. If Emily worked 360 days last year and took 8 vacation days in June and 4 more in December, how many additional vacation days can Emily still claim?

Emily is a huge fan of stickers and has a collection of colorful pens that she's willing to trade for them. A classmate offers to give Emily 6 stickers for each pen. On Monday, Emily brings 2 pens to trade. On Tuesday, she brings 3 more pens than she brought on Monday. On Wednesday, she brings half as many pens as she brought on Tuesday. If Emily uses 2 stickers each day for her journal, how many days will the stickers last?
Lionel walked 4 miles. Esther walked 975 yards and Niklaus walked 1287 feet. How many combined feet did the friends walk?

Lincoln Middle school competes in a volleyball tournament with Springfield Middle school. Lincoln Middle school scores 45 points in the first match, twice as much in the second match, and 20 points less than the second match in the third match. At the end of the tournament, Lincoln Middle school is awarded 75 bonus points and Springfield Middle school has 15 points less than Lincoln Middle school. How many points does Springfield Middle school have?

Ava has 6 hours to play video games and do her homework. She plays two video games that take 1.5 hours and 2 hours to complete. She then decides to work on her homework. If she can solve 5 math problems per minute, how many math problems does she solve before her free time is up?

Katie's mother wants to get granola bars for all the kids to eat after Katie's soccer game. There will be 30 kids playing soccer, including Katie. Katie's mother wants to get 2 granola bars for each kid, since the bars are not that big and she figures the kids will be very hungry. Each box of granola bars has 12 bars in it. How many boxes should Katie's mother buy?
Evelyn is a musician. She receives a $200 grant to support her music career. She performs at three concerts, earning $75 for each performance. How much money does she make in total from her music?
Michael is 4 times as heavy as his brother, while Daniel is 2 times as heavy as Michael. If Michael weighs 60kg, what is the weight difference between Daniel and Michael's brother?

Emily baked oatmeal raisin cookies for a bake sale, ensuring each cookie had exactly 9 raisins. She made 6 dozen in total. If she sells two-thirds of the cookies, how many raisins are left in the unsold cookies?

Tim's website got 100 visitors a day for the first 6 days and then on the last day of the week it got twice as many visitors as every other day combined.  If he gets $.01 per visit how much did he make that week?
Maya's garden has 18 cherry blossoms and her peach tree has 3 dozen peaches. How many more peaches does she have than cherry blossoms?
Alex studies for 8 hours a day, 6 days a week, to prepare for her exams. How many hours will she have studied in total after 3 months?
A water pump operating for 10 hours would consume 12 kilowatts. How many kilowatts would the water pump consume if it was used for 4 hours a day for 6 days?

Nancy is filling an aquarium for her fish. She fills it halfway and goes to answer the door. While she's gone, her cat knocks the aquarium over and spills half the water in it. Then Nancy comes back and triples the amount of water in the aquarium. If the aquarium is 4 feet long, 6 feet wide, and 3 feet high, how many cubic feet of water are in the aquarium?

Alex needs to hike 8 miles to reach the campsite. He can hike 2 miles per hour for three hours before taking a break, and then he can hike 0.5 miles per hour until he reaches the campsite. How long will it take Alex to reach the campsite?
Ava's cat sanctuary has 120 cats. She adopts out 30% of them but then receives 8 new cats that were rescued from a nearby neighborhood. How many cats does she have now?

In a library, there are 1800 books on the shelves. 720 of these books are fiction novels. The remaining books are either biographies or history books, with an equal number of each. How many history books are there in the library?

Lucas is building a tall tower using wooden blocks to test its stability. He begins by stacking 32 blocks on top of each other. The tower remains stable, so he adds 29 more blocks. As he continues to add more blocks, the tower eventually becomes unstable and collapses, totaling 91 blocks. How many additional blocks was Lucas able to add before the tower lost its balance and fell?

Olivia wants to make a protein shake with a total of 300 calories for her post-workout snack. A scoop of protein powder has 120 calories. A serving of almond milk has 60 calories. If she uses two scoops of protein powder, how many servings of almond milk should she add?
A concert is held at a stadium, and 350 people attend the first night. For the second night, twice as many people show up. If each ticket costs $30, how much did the concert make in total?

Ella and Lucas are working on a group project and need energy to finish on time. If Ella drinks 3 cups of tea per hour and Lucas drinks 2 times as much tea as Ella, calculate the total number of cups of tea they drink together in 4 hours.

Donny went to the gas station to gas up his tank. He knows his truck holds 150 liters of fuel. His truck already contained 38 liters. How much change will he get from $350 if each liter of fuel costs $3?

A forest has 350 trees. In a certain season, 15% of the trees fell due to strong winds in the first month, 30% of the remaining trees were cut down for logging by mid-season, and at the end of the season, another 40% of the trees that hadn't already fallen or been cut also fell due to a severe storm. How many trees are still standing at the end of the season?

Emily wants to buy a new tablet that costs $120. She already has $20 saved. She plans to walk her neighbor's dog to earn the rest of the money. If she walks the dog 8 times and has $10 left after buying the tablet, how much did she charge per dog walk?

A fruit vendor is preparing fruit baskets for a holiday sale. Each basket contains 12 pieces of fruit, and the vendor uses apples, bananas, grapes, and pineapples. This week, the vendor received 150 apples, 120 bananas, 180 grapes, and 100 pineapples. However, upon inspection, 20 apples, 30 bananas, 25 grapes, and 15 pineapples were found to be spoiled and unusable. How many fruit baskets can the vendor make for the holiday sale?

The school drama club sold 75 tickets to their play for $5 each and 30 concessions for $1 each. They used the money from their sales to rent a sound system that cost $200 and hire a lighting technician for $150. The rest of the money was used to buy 15 pizzas for the cast party. How much does a pizza cost?
Lily had 80 crayons. She gave half to her sister Mia. Mia then gave half of her crayons to their cousin Alex. Alex broke 8 crayons while coloring. How many crayons does Alex have left?

A container of four ice cream cones was left at room temperature and is slowly melting. Every time a cone melts, the remaining cones melt three times as fast as the previous one. How many times faster than the first cone does the last cone's remains melt?

Emily and Benjamin are planning a weekend getaway. A train ticket costs $30 for each person and a resort stay costs $15 for each person per night. How much money will they spend on the getaway if they stay for 2 nights?

Mia loves stickers and is willing to trade her favorite toys for them. A classmate knows that Mia has a collection of colorful pens that she treasures. She agrees to give Mia 6 stickers for each pen. On Monday, Mia brings her 4 pens. On Tuesday, she brings her 2 more pens than she brought on Monday. On Wednesday, she brings 2 fewer pens than she brought on Tuesday. If Mia uses 2 stickers a day, how many days will the stickers last?

Maya has a stamp collection that she enjoys expanding. She began with 75 stamps that her grandparents gave her. The following year, she tripled her collection. Over the next year, she added 2 new stamps each month. The year after that, she acquired 1 new stamp every other month. Unfortunately, the year after that, she lost a third of her stamps when her collection was damaged. How many stamps does Maya have left after the loss?

A bike shop has 36 bicycles and tricycles (in total) for sale. A quarter of the vehicles are tricycles, and a third of the bicycles have a bell included. If each bicycle has 2 wheels and each tricycle has 3 wheels, how many wheels are on the bike shop's vehicles in all?

Emily organized a bake sale to raise funds for a local animal shelter. Among all the baked goods she sold, four items accounted for 80% of the total sales. She sold a large chocolate cake for $50, a batch of cupcakes for one-fifth the price of the cake, a cheesecake for twice the price of the cake, and a fruit tart for three-fourths the price of the cheesecake. What is the total amount of money, in dollars, that Emily raised at the bake sale?

At a hotel, guests are being charged a resort fee without being informed. If my total bill was $220, the local tax rate is 12%, I booked a room for $120, and I had a breakfast for $20, how much did they charge me for the resort fee?

A manufacturing plant produced 9000 toy cars and their corresponding components last quarter. Each toy car came with 4 wheels, 1 steering wheel, 2 seats, and 3 decals. If it took 30 seconds to manufacture each toy car and 5 seconds to produce each component, what was the total machine operation time, in seconds, needed to make all the toy cars and their components?

A company is shipping boxes of books to a library. The maximum weight a delivery van can carry is 1200 kilograms. Each box of books weighs 15 kilograms. If there are 60 boxes of books to be shipped, how many more kilograms can still be loaded into the van?

Ana purchased 12 kilograms of flour for baking. She used one-third of it for croissants, one-quarter of it for muffins, and one-half of the remaining flour for bread. How many kilograms of flour are left after baking those three items?

Alex starts each week with $75, spends $20 every week and saves the rest. After several weeks, her aunt tripled her total savings and her grandmother gave her an additional $25. If she now has $900, how many weeks have elapsed?
Ashley learned that it's recommended to take a 5-minute break for every 60 minutes of studying. If Ashley spends 8 hours studying for her exams, how long will she spend taking breaks?

For 8 weeks in the fall, Alex buys himself a snack from the school cafeteria. Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday he gets a $2.50 bag of popcorn. Wednesday and Friday he gets a $1.75 granola bar. On the weekends, he treats himself to a $3.25 cinnamon roll. How much money does he spend on snacks in 8 weeks?

Two birds are chirping at each other from neighboring trees. The sparrow chirps three times for every one time the finch chirps. The finch's owner tries to calm it down every third time it chirps. She has to say "calm down" five times before the birds stopped chirping. How many times did the sparrow chirp?
Tom purchased 8 packs of blue pens with 15 pens in each pack. He also bought 6 packs of red pens with 20 pens in each pack. While unpacking, 8 blue pens were damaged. How many pens are left?
A bakery made a large cake that was cut into 24 pieces. At a party, five-sixths of the cake was eaten by the guests. How many pieces of cake were left?
Emily and Tom have a combined height of 150 inches. Tom is 8 inches more than triple Emily's height. How tall is Tom?

Mrs. Rodriguez owns a farm with 60 horses. Each horse consumes 120 kilograms of hay per day. She also has a goat ranch with 5 times the number of horses, with each goat eating 1/3 times as much hay as a horse does. How many kilograms of hay does Mrs. Rodriguez use to feed all of her animals in a month (assuming 30 days in a month)?

Mia and Alex want to see who can reach the top of a 30-story skyscraper first. Alex takes the stairs and can climb one floor in 12 seconds. Mia takes the elevator, which can travel one floor in 9 seconds, but it has a 2-second delay at every floor and an additional 5-second delay at every fifth floor. How long would it take for the slower one of Mia and Alex to reach the top floor?
Alex exercises at the gym 3 times more often than Emily does. If Emily goes to the gym 3 times per week, how many times will Alex go to the gym in 6 weeks?

Landon has 4 pencils. One pencil is 5 centimeters long. The second pencil is three times as long as the first, while the third pencil is 2 centimeters shorter than the second. The fourth pencil is 1 centimeter longer than the first pencil. What is the total length of Landon's pencils when they are put together?

There are 10 books on the table. Two-fifths of them are reading books and three-tenths of them are math books. There is one fewer science book than math books and the rest are history books. How many history books are there?

A concert hall has a capacity of 2,500 spectators, but tickets were only sold for 80% of the seats. Due to a traffic jam, 200 ticket holders were unable to attend the concert. How many people attended the concert?

Maya is a store clerk restocking shelves with boxes of cereal. In the breakfast aisle, she stocks 15 boxes. In the organic section, she stocks 22 boxes. In the discount section, she stocks 10 boxes but finds 6 that are expired and removes them from the shelves to return to the warehouse. She still has 20 boxes to stock. How many boxes of cereal did Maya start with?

Emily and Ryan want to buy their dad a $75.00 toolbox for Father's Day. Emily has $10.00 saved up and Ryan has $12.00. Emily then babysits 3 kids in her neighborhood, charging $8.00 per child, while Ryan washes 5 cars, charging $4.00 per car. How much more money will Emily and Ryan need to earn to buy the toolbox for their dad?

Flora has been experiencing frequent fractures. Dr. Juan has asked her to strengthen her bones by drinking 105 gallons of milk within 3 weeks. Flora thinks that drinking 3 gallons of milk daily will be enough, but her brother says she'll still need to drink more. To fulfill Dr. Juan’s requirement, how many more gallons must Flora drink daily?

Lily and Finn are preparing for a party. Lily has purchased 3 packs of balloons while Finn has bought 2 packs. Lily's packs each contain 4 red balloons and 6 blue balloons. Finn's packs have 5 red balloons and 7 blue balloons. How many balloons do Lily and Finn have in total?
Emily decides to sell 75% of her paintings. She bought them for $15 each and sells them for $25 each. If she had 160 paintings, how much more money did she have compared to before she bought them?

Emily starts swimming for exercise. She burns three times as many calories per hour as she did when she was jogging. She swims three times a week, with each session lasting 45 minutes, and she does this for 6 weeks. If she burned 200 calories an hour jogging, how many calories will she burn in total from swimming over the 6 weeks?
Maya is 3 inches shorter than Ava, who is 5 inches taller than Julian. If Samantha is 58 inches tall and has the same height as Ava, calculate the average height of the four people.
Alex and Ben went on a cycling tour for 4 days. Each day, Alex had to cycle 10 hours and Ben had to cycle 5 hours to reach their campsite. How many hours did they cycle altogether?

Evelyn inherited $25000 from her great aunt and decided to handle her newfound wealth responsibly. She put a quarter of the inheritance towards buying a new home, then allocated a fifth of the remaining amount to pay off her credit card debt. She put $2000 in an emergency fund and invested a tenth of that amount in a retirement account. How many dollars does Evelyn have left for discretionary spending?
Samantha is 3 years older than Olivia. Olivia is 12 years younger than Ava. Ava is 3 times older than Ethan. If Ethan is 15, how old is Samantha?
Emily writes 8 pages of her journal on weekdays and 15 pages on weekends. If she keeps writing for 3 weeks, how many pages will her journal have?

Janet lives in a city built on a grid system.  She walks 3 blocks north, then seven times as many blocks west. Then she turns around and walks 8 blocks south and twice as many blocks east in the direction of her home. If Janet can walk 2 blocks/minute, how long will it take her to get home?
There are 8 more yellow bananas than purple bananas in a fruit basket. There are 15 purple bananas. How many bananas are there in the fruit basket?

Emily drives 25 miles from her house to the beach. After spending some time at the beach, she heads to her friend's place. To get to her friend's place, she travels for 45 minutes at 15 miles per hour. How many miles in total does Emily travel?

Alex purchased a box of granola bars and ate two-thirds of the box on the first day. The next day, he ate one-third of the remaining granola bars. He has 12 granola bars left on the third day. How many granola bars were in the box initially?

In a library, there are 18 shelves of books. Three-eighths of them are fiction books, and two-sevenths of them are non-fiction books. The number of biography books is two more than the non-fiction books, and the rest are self-help books. How many self-help books are there?
Gabriel the Blacksmith has $35 worth of silver bars. He sells 5 silver bars to Alexander. After he is paid, he has $20. How many silver bars does Gabriel have left?

A university has 800 students enrolled in a specific program. Due to budget cuts, there will be two rounds of reductions. For each round, 12% of the remaining students will be required to transfer to another program. How many students will be required to transfer in total?

Tom's grandfather has $15,000 to divide among his three grandchildren. Tom will receive one-third of the money, as he is the eldest. Alex will get 55 percent of the remaining amount, and Ben will receive the leftover money. How much money will Ben get?

A professional StarCraft II coach is analyzing the performance of a player over a series of matches. The player has been practicing a strategy that involves balancing resource collection (minerals and gas) and unit production efficiency. The coach notices that the player's mineral collection rate can be modeled by the polynomial equation \( M(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 1 \), where \( x \) represents the number of minutes into the game.

1. The player needs to determine when the mineral collection rate first exceeds 50 minerals per minute. Formulate and solve the inequality \( M(x) > 50 \) to find the smallest integer value of \( x \) that satisfies this condition.

2. Additionally, the coach observes that the player's unit production efficiency can be described by the quadratic equation \( U(y) = -3y^2 + 12y \), where \( y \) represents the number of units produced. The coach wants to find the range of \( y \) for which the production efficiency is at least 18. Set up and solve the inequality \( U(y) \geq 18 \) to find the possible values of \( y \).

As an aspiring human resources professional interested in board composition and diversity, you are analyzing the board of directors for a corporation. The board currently has 12 members, and you want to ensure that the board's diversity reflects the company's goal of having at least 40% of the members represent minority groups.

1. If the current board has \( x \) members representing minority groups, write an inequality to determine the minimum number of minority group members required to meet the company's diversity goal. Solve the inequality for \( x \).

2. The company plans to expand the board by adding 4 more members, all of whom must be from minority groups to improve diversity. After the addition, the percentage of board members from minority groups should be at least 50%. Let \( y \) represent the total number of minority group members after the addition. Write an equation to represent this situation and solve for \( y \).

As a proud lifelong resident of Trenton, New Jersey, you are interested in planning a new community park. The city plans to build a rectangular garden within the park, and the area of this garden will be represented by the polynomial expression \( A(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x \), where \( x \) is a measure in meters related to the garden's dimensions.

1. If the desired area of the garden is 60 square meters, find the possible values of \( x \) by solving the equation \( 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x = 60 \).

2. Additionally, a walking path will run diagonally across the garden. If the length of the diagonal is given by the expression \( \sqrt{x^2 + (2x)^2} \), simplify this expression to its most reduced form.

As the editor of a British history magazine, you are tasked with preparing a special edition that celebrates key historical events from two different centuries. You plan to divide the magazine into two sections: one dedicated to the 19th century and the other to the 20th century. 

1. You decide that the number of pages dedicated to the 19th-century section should be a quadratic function of the form \( p(n) = an^2 + bn + c \), where \( n \) is the number of significant events covered from that century. If you plan to cover 8 significant events, and know that the section should have 32 pages when \( n = 4 \) and 72 pages when \( n = 6 \), determine the quadratic function \( p(n) \).

2. Additionally, you want the 20th-century section to have at least 50 pages, but no more than twice the pages of the 19th-century section calculated for 12 significant events. Write and solve an inequality to find the possible range for the number of pages in the 20th-century section.

As a software developer who loves classical music, you are designing a new feature for your music notation app that allows users to generate visually appealing sheet music. You decide to use your coding skills to model the layout of musical notes on a staff using mathematical equations.

1. To represent the position of a note on the staff, you use a polynomial equation. The x-axis represents the time, while the y-axis represents the vertical position of the note. The polynomial you use is given by \( P(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 7 \). You need to ensure that the notes do not exceed a certain height on the staff to maintain readability. Solve the inequality \( P(x) \leq 10 \) to find the range of x-values where the notes remain within the allowed height.

2. In addition to the layout, you want to ensure that the duration between consecutive notes (represented as x-values) is optimized for smooth playback. You model the duration between notes using the quadratic equation \( D(x) = x^2 - 4x + 3 \). Determine the x-values where the duration is zero, which would indicate overlapping notes, by solving the equation \( D(x) = 0 \).

As a parole board member, you are analyzing data from a research study conducted by a professor who found a mathematical model to predict the likelihood of parole success based on various factors. The model is represented by the quadratic equation:

\[ S(x) = -0.5x^2 + 4x + 3 \]

where \( S(x) \) represents the success score for parole, and \( x \) is the number of years since the parolee was released. 

1. Determine the maximum success score and the corresponding number of years since release by finding the vertex of the parabola described by the quadratic equation.

2. The study suggests that a success score of at least 7 is considered satisfactory. Find the range of years \( x \) for which the success score \( S(x) \) is at least 7.

A state senator is drafting a new piece of legislation that requires the calculation of fines for legal violations. The senator consults with a judge who suggests that the fines should be calculated based on a quadratic formula to account for the severity of the violation. The fine, \( F \), in dollars, is given by the function \( F(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \), where \( x \) represents the severity level of the violation on a scale from 1 to 10, and \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \) are constants.

1. After consulting with the judge, the senator decides that for severity level 2, the fine should be $50, and for severity level 5, the fine should be $150. Moreover, the fine for severity level 0 should be $20 (this represents some base administrative cost). Set up the system of equations based on these conditions and find the values of \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \).

2. Once the senator has determined the values of \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \), they realize that the fines should not exceed $500 regardless of severity levels. Determine the inequality that represents this condition and find the range of severity levels \( x \) for which the fine does not exceed $500.

As a financial translation specialist focusing on regulatory financial statements, you often encounter various polynomial models predicting the performance of a company's stock based on market conditions. One such model is given by the polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 5x - 7 \), where \( x \) represents the market index level in hundreds, and \( P(x) \) represents the predicted percentage change in the stock price.

1. A regulatory agency requires you to ensure that the predicted percentage change in the stock price does not exceed 5%. Determine the range of \( x \) values for which this condition is satisfied.

2. During a translation of a financial statement, you encounter a situation where the predicted percentage change was mistakenly recorded as \( P(x) = 0 \). Find the market index levels, \( x \), at which this error could have occurred.

As a military officer studying military history, you are analyzing the trajectory of a historical projectile fired during a famous battle. The projectile follows a parabolic path described by the equation \( h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 50t + 10 \), where \( h(t) \) is the height in meters and \( t \) is the time in seconds.

1. Determine the time at which the projectile reaches its maximum height and calculate this maximum height.

2. During your analysis, you find that the projectile needs to clear a wall that is 30 meters tall. Calculate the time intervals during which the projectile is above 30 meters.

As a Brazilian parent reflecting on your childhood, you remember shopping for toys at Ri Happy, where you often bought toy cars and action figures. Now, you want to recreate that experience for your child. Let's say a toy car costs 20 BRL and an action figure costs 35 BRL. You decide to buy a total of 12 toys, spending exactly 340 BRL.

1. Write a system of linear equations to represent the number of toy cars (x) and action figures (y) you purchased. How many of each did you buy?

2. After verifying the cost of toys, you realize there is a discount on toy cars. Each toy car now costs 15 BRL. If you still want to buy the same number of toys (12), how much would you spend in total? Write and solve a new equation to find the new total cost.

Pastor John often uses his experiences to illustrate how small positive influences can exponentially impact society. He observes that if he inspires 3 new people each year, and each of those people inspires another 3 new people in the following year, the number of people positively influenced grows exponentially.

1. Suppose the number of people Pastor John inspires each year can be modeled by the polynomial function \( P(n) = 3 \times 3^n \), where \( n \) represents the number of years since Pastor John began his work. Calculate the number of people directly or indirectly influenced by the end of the 4th year.

2. Pastor John also notes that there is a saturation point in the community, such that the maximum number of people who can be influenced is 300. Determine the smallest integer value of \( n \) for which the number of people influenced exceeds the saturation point, by solving the inequality \( 3^n > 100 \).

An influencer spends "x" hours on social media each day. Their sibling suggests they take breaks to improve their mental well-being, recommending that they reduce their social media usage by 30% and spend an additional 2 hours per day on relaxing activities. 

1. If the influencer initially spends 10 hours per day on social media, express their new daily routine in terms of a polynomial equation. Let "y" represent the total hours spent on social media and relaxing activities combined.

2. Solve for y given the initial condition, and determine the percentage increase or decrease in the total time spent compared to the original 10 hours of social media usage.

As a data analyst, you are working on a dataset in Google Sheets that tracks the monthly sales data for a company. The sales data for the last 4 months (in thousands of dollars) can be modeled by the polynomial function \( f(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 3 \), where \( x \) represents the month number starting from January (i.e., January is \( x=1 \), February is \( x=2 \), etc.).

1. Determine the months in which the sales data exactly matched the company's target of 0 thousand dollars. In other words, solve the equation \( f(x) = 0 \) to find the month numbers.

2. After finding the months from part 1, suppose the company wants to adjust its target to ensure sales are at least 2 thousand dollars. Represent this new condition as an inequality and determine for which month numbers \( x \) the adjusted sales target is met based on the function \( f(x) \).

A sports commentator is analyzing the statistics of a basketball game. During the game, a Chinese player scored points with his jersey number, which is a polynomial number in Chinese that the commentator cannot understand. The commentator only knows that the player's jersey number is a three-digit number where the hundreds digit is twice the tens digit, and the sum of all the digits equals 9. 

1. If the polynomial representation of the number is expressed as \( x^2 + 2xy + y^2 \), where \( x \) is the hundreds digit and \( y \) is the tens digit, find the digits of the player's jersey number.

2. After the game, the commentator realizes that the player's total score was equal to the cube of the tens digit of his jersey number reduced by 7. If the score was 27, verify the solution from the first sub-problem by solving this equation.

As an expert RV mechanic, you are tasked with optimizing the fuel efficiency of a particular RV model. This model's fuel efficiency is directly affected by the weight of the vehicle and the efficiency of the engine, which can be represented by the following equations.

1. The weight of the RV (in pounds) is modeled by the polynomial equation \( W(x) = 2000 + 150x - 5x^2 \), where \( x \) is the number of additional upgrades installed on the RV. Determine the number of upgrades, \( x \), that will maximize the weight of the RV. Use this value of \( x \) to find the maximum weight.

2. Additionally, the engine efficiency, \( E(x) \), is inversely proportional to the square root of the weight of the RV and is given by \( E(x) = \frac{600}{\sqrt{W(x)}} \). Using the value of \( x \) found in the first part, calculate the engine efficiency at this maximum weight.

The baseball team managed by the fiery team manager is in a season-long rivalry with another team led by the persona. The manager decides to use statistics to analyze the team's performance and strategize for the upcoming games.

1. The manager notices that the number of home runs (H) their team hits in a game can be modeled by the polynomial equation \( H(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 4 \), where \( x \) represents the number of games played in a week. Find the number of games \( x \) for which the team hits exactly 10 home runs in a week.

2. The manager wants to ensure that the ratio of the team's total home runs to the number of games played in a week is at least 3. Simplify the expression for this ratio using the equation \( H(x) \) from sub-problem 1, and set up an inequality to determine the minimum number of games \( x \) the team must play in a week to achieve this ratio.

1. The former political figure, seeking a peaceful life, decides to invest in a secluded property. The area of the property is modeled by the polynomial \( A(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x - 7 \), where \( x \) represents the number of years since the purchase. After a few years, the figure realizes that the property is not as calming as hoped, and they want to sell it when the area reaches 1000 square units. Solve for \( x \) when \( A(x) = 1000 \).

2. To ensure the property remains undisturbed by the public, the former political figure also needs to construct a fence around the property. The cost of the fence in dollars is modeled by the quadratic equation \( C(y) = 4y^2 - 12y + 9 \), where \( y \) is the length of the side of the square property. Determine the values of \( y \) that minimize the cost of the fence.

A renowned event industry blogger and speaker is planning a series of promotional events for a beverage brand's partnership initiatives. The blogger has decided to host two types of events: workshops and webinars.

1. The cost of organizing each workshop is represented by the polynomial \( C(w) = 5w^2 + 3w + 200 \), where \( w \) is the number of workshops. The budget allocated for the workshops is $3000. Formulate and solve the inequality to find the maximum number of workshops the blogger can organize without exceeding the budget.

2. For each webinar, the expected number of attendees can be modeled by a quadratic equation \( A(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 20 \), where \( x \) is the amount of money (in hundreds of dollars) spent on marketing. Determine the optimal amount of money the blogger should spend on marketing to maximize the number of attendees per webinar.

A documentary filmmaker is planning a series about haunted locations and wants to capture the eerie atmosphere of a mysterious old mansion. The filmmaker knows that the number of eerie shots, \( E \), they can capture is modeled by the quadratic equation \( E = -2t^2 + 12t \), where \( t \) represents the number of hours spent filming.

1. Determine the number of hours \( t \) that will maximize the number of eerie shots captured. What is the maximum number of eerie shots?

2. While filming, the filmmaker encounters technical difficulties and needs to adjust the camera settings, which reduces the number of eerie shots by a factor of \( \frac{1}{3t} \). Write the expression for the new number of eerie shots, and determine the value of \( t \) when the eerie shots are reduced to at least half of the maximum eerie shots found in the previous part.

Hermenegildo Portocarrero led his troops in a series of campaigns during the Paraguayan War. Suppose an amateur historian is researching these campaigns and discovers that one of the battles took place in a region where the troop numbers followed a specific pattern over time. The historian models the troop numbers using a polynomial equation based on accounts from his ancestor.

1. If the number of troops \( T \) at time \( t \) in days is given by the polynomial equation \( T(t) = 3t^3 - 5t^2 + 7t + 150 \), find the time \( t \) when the number of troops was exactly 200.

2. The historian also discovers that the troop numbers never fell below a certain amount during the campaign. If the minimum number of troops is described by the inequality \( 3t^2 - t + 10 \geq 0 \), determine the range of days \( t \) during which this condition was met.

Piotr is organizing a music festival dedicated to Eastern European composers. One of his favorite composers, Frédéric Chopin, inspires him to create a playlist for the event featuring both polonaises and mazurkas. The number of polonaises, \( p \), and the number of mazurkas, \( m \), must satisfy the following conditions:

1. The total number of pieces in the playlist is 36, which can be expressed as the equation \( p + m = 36 \).
2. Piotr wants the playlist to reflect the ratio of polonaises to mazurkas that mirrors Chopin's own compositions. Suppose Chopin composed 50 polonaises and 57 mazurkas. Set up the equation \( \frac{p}{m} = \frac{50}{57} \).

Find the number of polonaises and mazurkas in Piotr's playlist.

Sub-problem:

After finalizing the playlist, Piotr decides to perform further analysis on the music pieces' durations. If the average duration of a polonaise is 7 minutes and that of a mazurka is 3 minutes, express the total duration \( D \) of the playlist as a function of \( p \), and calculate the total duration using the values found for \( p \) and \( m \).

An architecture professor is designing a small pavilion inspired by the works of Robert A.M. Stern. The pavilion's roof is to be a parabolic arch, modeled by the quadratic function \( f(x) = -2x^2 + 8x + 10 \), where \( f(x) \) represents the height of the arch above the ground in feet, and \( x \) is the horizontal distance in feet from one end of the arch.

1. Determine the maximum height of the arch and the distance from the starting point of the arch to where this maximum height occurs.

2. The professor also wants to ensure that the height of the arch is at least 6 feet across a central span of the pavilion. Find the horizontal distance over which the height of the arch is at least 6 feet.

Professor Numis, a renowned expert in numismatics, is studying a collection of ancient coins. In his collection, he has two types of coins: silver coins and gold coins. The total number of coins in his collection is 150. The value of each silver coin is $20, while the value of each gold coin is $50. The total value of all the coins is $5,000.

1. Create a system of linear equations that represents the number of silver and gold coins in Professor Numis's collection. Use this system to determine how many silver coins and how many gold coins are in the collection.

2. Professor Numis decides to add more coins to his collection. He plans to add 10 more gold coins and an unknown number of silver coins. If the total value of the collection after adding these coins should be $6,200, how many silver coins must he add?

A successful Russian artist named Ivan moved to a new country and decided to open an art studio. To fund his studio, Ivan sold several pieces of art, priced differently based on their uniqueness and the effort involved. He sold two types of paintings: landscape paintings and abstract paintings.

1. The price of a landscape painting is modeled by the polynomial function \( P(x) = 3x^3 - 5x^2 + 2x + 100 \), where \( x \) is the number of hours spent on the painting. If Ivan spent 4 hours on a particular landscape painting, what was the selling price of that painting?

2. Ivan noticed that the demand for his abstract paintings can be modeled by the quadratic equation \( D(y) = -2y^2 + 12y + 36 \), where \( y \) is the number of abstract paintings sold, and \( D(y) \) is the profit in hundreds of dollars. What is the maximum profit Ivan can achieve, and how many abstract paintings must he sell to reach this maximum profit?

A newlywed couple, Alex and Maria, are planning to reunite with their families in their home country. They need to save enough money for the immigration process, which includes application fees and travel expenses. They decide to save money in a joint savings account, starting with an initial deposit. Their goal is to reach a total savings amount of $15,000 in 12 months.

1. Alex and Maria together save $400 each month. They also decide to make an initial deposit of $D. Write a linear equation that represents the total amount in their savings account, A(t), after t months. How much should the initial deposit be so that they reach their target of $15,000 in 12 months?

2. In addition to their monthly savings, they expect to receive a one-time financial gift from a family member after 6 months, which will also be added to their savings account. If they anticipate the gift to be $G and want the total amount in their savings account to still be $15,000 by the end of 12 months, determine the relationship between D and G, assuming their monthly savings remain unchanged.

As a tourism manager, you are responsible for maintaining safety standards at a popular tourist site with a scenic overlook. The safety guidelines require that the number of visitors on the overlook at any time should not exceed a maximum capacity, which is determined by a polynomial equation based on the structural integrity of the overlook. The equation for the maximum number of visitors \( V \) is given by:

\[ V^3 - 6V^2 + 11V - 6 = 0 \]

Sub-problem 1: Solve the polynomial equation to find the possible maximum capacities \( V \) that satisfy the safety guidelines. 

Sub-problem 2: If the current number of visitors on the overlook is represented by \( x \), and to ensure safety, the inequality \( x \leq V - 1 \) must be satisfied at all times. Using one of the solutions for \( V \) from sub-problem 1, solve the inequality to determine the maximum number of additional visitors allowed on the overlook.

An enforcement officer in a nature reserve is planning to use geospatial data to optimize patrol routes and identify potential poaching hotspots. The reserve is divided into sections, and the officer has identified that the risk of poaching in each section depends on the proximity to a river and the amount of dense forest cover.

1. The risk factor \( R(x) \) for poaching in a section is modeled by the quadratic equation \( R(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 3 \), where \( x \) represents the distance in kilometers from the river. Determine the distance from the river that maximizes the risk of poaching. What is the maximum risk factor?

2. The officer also needs to ensure that the risk factor remains above 7 for effective monitoring. Using the equation from part 1, find the range of distances from the river where the risk factor \( R(x) \) is greater than 7.

A corporate trainer is planning a series of orientation sessions for new employees. The trainer conducts sessions in two phases: Phase A focuses on company policies, and Phase B focuses on integration activities. Each session in Phase A lasts for 2 hours, while each session in Phase B lasts for 1.5 hours. The trainer has scheduled a total of 10 sessions, and the total duration of all sessions combined is 18 hours.

1. Formulate a system of equations to represent the number of sessions in Phase A and Phase B. Solve the system to find out how many sessions of each type the trainer has scheduled.

2. The trainer wants to ensure that each new employee attends at least one session from both phases. If there are 5 new employees and each session can accommodate a maximum of 3 employees, determine the minimum number of additional sessions required in each phase to ensure all new employees can attend at least one session from both phases.

A young aspiring Malayalam poet from Thiruvananthapuram is organizing poetry readings in various parts of the city. She plans to visit a number of libraries and cafes to share her work. She decides to split her time between writing new poems and practicing her readings. Let the number of hours she spends writing new poems in a week be denoted by \( x \), and the number of hours she spends practicing her readings be denoted by \( y \).

1. She finds that the total number of hours she spends on both activities in a week is 24 hours. Additionally, she wants to spend at least twice as many hours writing as she does practicing. Write a system of inequalities that represents these conditions.

2. Suppose she also wants to ensure that she spends no less than 8 hours and no more than 18 hours writing new poems each week. Given this additional constraint, find the possible range of hours she can spend practicing her readings.

A travel blogger who spent her childhood in Indiana decides to document her journey across the United States. She plans to visit a series of landmarks, starting her trip in Indianapolis. Her first stop after Indianapolis is at a landmark that is 150 miles away. She continues to travel to other landmarks, each time traveling a distance that is 50 miles more than the previous leg of her journey.

1. Write a quadratic equation to determine the total number of stops (including the first stop) she can make if she plans to travel a total of 1500 miles on this trip. 

2. If she covers these distances at an average speed of 60 miles per hour, calculate the total time in hours she will spend traveling during this trip.

You and your fellow cyclist often ride together on Oxford Road, which is 12 kilometers long. You both decide to have a friendly race along this road. Your speed is \( x \) kilometers per hour, and your fellow cyclist's speed is \( x + 2 \) kilometers per hour because they have been training more.

1. Write a rational expression for the time it takes for you to complete the 12-kilometer ride. Then, write a similar expression for your fellow cyclist.

2. If your fellow cyclist finishes the ride 0.5 hours before you, set up an equation based on the expressions from part 1 and solve for \( x \) to find your respective cycling speeds.

As an architectural historian, you are analyzing two buildings from the Gothic period and are particularly interested in their pointed arches, which are a hallmark of this architectural style. You have found two different pointed arches with parabolic shapes and are tasked with determining some geometric properties that align with their historical design principles.

1. The first arch has a height that reaches its maximum at 20 meters and spans a width of 30 meters at the base. The equation of the parabola representing this arch can be expressed in vertex form as \( y = a(x - h)^2 + k \). Find the value of \( a \), given that the vertex of the parabola is at the maximum height, and determine the equation of the parabola.

2. The second arch is known to have a base width of 24 meters and a height of 18 meters at its vertex. The equation for this parabola can be expressed in standard form as \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \). Assuming that the parabola is symmetric about the y-axis, find the coefficients \( a \), \( b \), and \( c \) for this quadratic equation.

As a medical school student, you're keeping track of your study hours for the MCAT and your volunteer hours at the local hospital. You find that balancing these activities is similar to solving a system of equations.

1. Suppose you study for the MCAT twice as many hours as you volunteer each week. If the total number of hours spent on both activities is 18 hours per week, how many hours do you study and volunteer each week? Formulate and solve a system of equations to find the solution.

2. In preparation for the upcoming exams, you decide to adjust your schedule. You want to increase your study hours by 50% and decrease your volunteer hours by 2 hours, which results in a total of 20 hours spent on both activities. Based on your new schedule, how many hours will you now study and volunteer each week?

An author of young adult fantasy novels, who promotes reading through book talks, noticed that the number of attendees at her book talks can be modeled by the quadratic equation \( n(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 20 \), where \( n(x) \) represents the number of attendees and \( x \) is the number of book talks given in a month. The author wants to maximize her reach and is planning her schedule for the next month.

1. Determine the maximum number of attendees she can expect in a single month by finding the vertex of the quadratic equation.

2. To increase her engagement, the author decides to give additional online talks. If she gives \( y \) online talks, the total number of attendees, including both in-person and online, is doubled. Write an inequality representing the number of online talks \( y \) she should give to ensure that the total number of attendees exceeds 100, based on the maximum number of in-person attendees you found in part 1.

A veterinarian specializing in small pets has a unique way of organizing her pet care routine at home. She notices that the time she spends caring for her two dogs is represented by the polynomial \( 2x^2 + 3x + 5 \) minutes per day, where \( x \) represents the number of extra tasks she has on a given day. For her three cats, the time is represented by the polynomial \( x^2 + 4x + 2 \) minutes per day. 

1. Find the polynomial that represents the total time she spends caring for all her pets in terms of \( x \).

2. If on a particular day she has 2 extra tasks (i.e., \( x = 2 \)), determine whether she can complete all her pet care tasks in under 30 minutes. Use the polynomial you found in the first part to decide this.

As an environmental policy maker, you propose a new strategy for biodiversity conservation that includes planting native trees in a protected area. You and your sibling, who prefers a different strategy, have a friendly debate about which method would increase biodiversity the fastest. To model the growth of biodiversity using your method, you use the polynomial function \( B(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 3x + 10 \), where \( B(x) \) represents the biodiversity index after \( x \) years. Your sibling models their method with the quadratic function \( S(x) = -x^2 + 6x + 8 \).

1. Determine the number of years it will take for both methods to result in the same biodiversity index by solving the equation \( B(x) = S(x) \).

2. Calculate the biodiversity index for each method at the point where they are equal.

A skilled operative has intercepted a coded message that gives a clue about the number of double agents in their organization. The message is expressed as a polynomial equation where \( x \) represents the number of double agents. The equation is given as follows:

\[ 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 4 = 0 \]

1. Solve the polynomial equation to determine the potential number of double agents.

Additionally, the operative knows that the maximum number of double agents they can handle at once without compromising their mission is a value that satisfies the inequality:

\[ 3x - 5 < 2x + 7 \]

2. Determine the maximum number of double agents the operative can handle based on the inequality.

The grandchild is writing a simple code to simulate the trajectory of a ball thrown upwards with an initial velocity. The professor suggests using the physics formula for the height of the ball at any time \( t \): \( h(t) = -16t^2 + vt + s \), where \( v \) is the initial velocity in feet per second, and \( s \) is the initial height in feet.

1. Suppose the grandchild wants the ball to reach a maximum height of 50 feet. If the initial velocity \( v \) is 32 feet per second and the ball is thrown from a height of 5 feet, determine the time \( t \) when the ball reaches its maximum height.

2. Additionally, the grandchild wants to ensure that the ball does not go over the height of 50 feet. Using the same initial conditions, determine the range of time \( t \) during which the ball is at or below 50 feet in height.

A legendary film producer, known for his successes and heated debates about creativity, has decided to produce a new movie. The movie's success is modeled by the polynomial equation \( S(x) = -2x^3 + 5x^2 + 3x + 20 \), where \( S(x) \) represents the success score of the movie (in arbitrary units) and \( x \) represents the creativity level of the production team, on a scale from 0 to 10.

1. Determine the creativity level \( x \) that maximizes the movie's success score. Assume that \( x \) can only be a whole number.

2. After a heated debate, the producer decides to increase the creativity level by 2 units, but the budget constraints impose that the success score should not exceed 50 units. Determine the range of creativity levels \( x \) in which this condition holds, considering the new creativity level.

As the IT director at a university, you are tasked with optimizing the bandwidth allocation for the research department to ensure smooth technology implementation. The total bandwidth available is 2000 Mbps, which is currently distributed among three types of research projects: data analysis, virtual simulations, and machine learning.

1. The bandwidth for data analysis projects is twice that allocated to virtual simulations. The machine learning projects require 300 Mbps more than the virtual simulations. Write a system of equations to represent this situation and determine how much bandwidth is allocated to each type of project.

2. Due to new research demands, you need to increase the bandwidth for machine learning projects by 50%. This increase requires you to redistribute the total bandwidth, but the new allocation must still satisfy the original condition that the bandwidth for data analysis is twice that of virtual simulations. Determine the new bandwidth allocation for each type of project.

Dr. Adeyemi, a dedicated Nigerian academic and member of the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), is analyzing the distribution of research grants among different departments in his university. He notices that if the total amount of research grants (in millions of Naira) available for distribution is modeled by the polynomial \( P(x) = 4x^3 - 15x^2 + 9x - 10 \), where \( x \) represents the number of departments applying for grants, then:

1. Determine the number of departments \( x \) for which the research grants polynomial \( P(x) \) equals zero. This involves solving the polynomial equation \( 4x^3 - 15x^2 + 9x - 10 = 0 \).

2. If Dr. Adeyemi wants to ensure that each department receives at least 0.5 million Naira, determine the range of \( x \) (the number of departments) for which the average grant per department, \( \frac{P(x)}{x} \geq 0.5 \), is true. This involves solving the inequality \( \frac{4x^3 - 15x^2 + 9x - 10}{x} \geq 0.5 \).

An ambassador is organizing a series of international law seminars to foster political solutions among nations. She plans to host these seminars in two phases: an initial series and a follow-up series. The total number of seminars is represented by the polynomial \( P(x) = 2x^2 + 3x - 5 \), where \( x \) is some positive integer representing a factor related to international law, such as the number of nations involved.

1. Determine the number of seminars she can conduct if the positive factor \( x = 3 \).

2. Due to unforeseen circumstances, the ambassador needs to reduce the total number of seminars by 10%. Create an inequality to represent the new total number of seminars and solve for the possible values of \( x \) that satisfy this condition.

Dr. Harper is a compassionate physician who manages the healthcare needs of a couple, Mr. and Mrs. Lewis, and monitors their medication schedules. Mr. Lewis requires medication every 4 hours, while Mrs. Lewis takes a different medication every 6 hours. 

1. Dr. Harper wants to find the times of the day, within a 24-hour period, when both Mr. and Mrs. Lewis need to take their medications simultaneously. Represent this situation with a system of equations and find the solution.

2. Additionally, Dr. Harper tracks the couple's health-related expenses. If Mr. Lewis's medication costs $8 per dose and Mrs. Lewis's medication costs $10 per dose, and their combined medication expenses for one day must not exceed $100, express this constraint as an inequality and determine if it's possible for them to stay within budget given their medication schedules.

A journalist is analyzing the impact of speeches on society by examining the number of views a speech recording receives online. They have noticed that the number of views, \( V(t) \), of a particular speech increases according to the quadratic function \( V(t) = -2t^2 + 16t + 32 \), where \( t \) is the number of days since the speech was uploaded.

1. Determine the day \( t \) on which the speech recording receives the maximum number of views. What is the maximum number of views?

2. After how many days will the speech recording have exactly 100 views? (Assume the views follow the same quadratic function.)

A young adult fiction author is researching historical events for their next novel. They spend their time between two libraries, Library A and Library B, each offering unique historical archives. The author plans to spend a total of 14 hours in both libraries over the weekend. At Library A, they find that for every hour spent researching, they gather 3 unique historical perspectives. At Library B, every hour spent results in 5 unique historical perspectives. 

1. Let \( x \) represent the number of hours spent at Library A, and \( y \) represent the number of hours spent at Library B. Write a system of equations based on the information given, and solve for \( x \) and \( y \) if the author wants to gather exactly 58 unique historical perspectives over the weekend.

2. After spending time in both libraries, the author decides to write a fictional story using the historical perspectives gathered. They estimate that for every unique historical perspective, they will write approximately 2 pages. If the author has already written 12 pages of the novel, how many total pages will the novel be once they incorporate all the perspectives gathered from both libraries?

An economist is analyzing the effects of electric vehicle (EV) tax incentives on the energy market. Suppose the demand \( D(x) \) for EVs in thousands of units is modeled by the quadratic equation \( D(x) = -2x^2 + 12x + 50 \), where \( x \) represents the tax incentive in thousands of dollars. The supply \( S(x) \) is modeled by the linear equation \( S(x) = 4x + 30 \).

1. Determine the value of the tax incentive \( x \) that equalizes supply and demand for EVs. 

2. For the value of \( x \) found in the first sub-problem, calculate the corresponding number of EVs in thousands that would be supplied and demanded.

An artist named Aiko lives in a distant country known for its beautiful landscapes and rich cultural heritage. Aiko is inspired by these surroundings to create a piece of art in the shape of a large mural. The mural is rectangular and its length is 3 meters longer than twice its width. The total area of the mural is 60 square meters.

1. Set up and solve a quadratic equation to find the dimensions (length and width) of the mural.

Aiko also plans to add a decorative border around the mural. The border has a uniform width and increases the total area of the mural and border to 84 square meters.

2. Set up and solve an equation to determine the width of the border.

During the Renaissance period in the Dalmatian region, an ancient scroll was found in a historical archive. This scroll contains a polynomial equation that describes the number of significant cultural events, \( E(x) \), that occurred in the region over a certain number of decades, \( x \). The equation is given by:

\[ E(x) = 2x^3 - 9x^2 + 12x - 4 \]

1. Determine the number of decades after the beginning of the Renaissance period when the number of cultural events reached a local maximum. To do this, find the critical points of the polynomial and check the nature of these points.

2. Legend has it that a particularly grand event occurred during a decade when the number of cultural events, \( E(x) \), was exactly 20. Solve for the decade, \( x \), when this event might have occurred by solving the equation \( E(x) = 20 \).

A local artist creates fan art inspired by their favorite TV shows and sells them at the comic book store. The artist has noticed that the number of pieces they sell is related to the popularity of the TV shows, and they want to model this relationship with a quadratic equation. 

1. The artist finds that when they produce art for a show with a popularity rating of 3, they sell 15 pieces, and for a show with a popularity rating of 5, they sell 35 pieces. Furthermore, when the popularity rating is 7, they sell 63 pieces. Assuming the number of pieces sold \( S(x) \) is a quadratic function of the popularity rating \( x \), find the quadratic equation \( S(x) = ax^2 + bx + c \).

2. Once the equation is found, the artist wants to maximize their sales. Determine the popularity rating that would yield the maximum number of art pieces sold, and calculate the maximum number of pieces sold using the quadratic model.

A travel agent specializing in customizing itineraries for travelers with disabilities is planning a trip to a city with a new accessible transportation system. The system includes buses and trains, both designed to accommodate travelers with various disabilities. The agent needs to determine the optimal number of bus rides and train rides to recommend to maximize the travel experience within a given budget.

1. The cost of a bus ride is $3, and the cost of a train ride is $5. If the total budget for transportation is $60, and the agent wants to ensure that travelers take at least twice as many bus rides as train rides, how many bus rides (b) and train rides (t) should be included in the itinerary? Write and solve the system of inequalities to find the possible values for b and t.

2. Additionally, the travel agent knows that the travelers should spend at least four hours in total on transportation, with a bus ride taking 30 minutes and a train ride taking 45 minutes. Write and solve the inequality to find the possible values for b and t that satisfy this condition.

As fellow graduate students interested in geometric topology, you are investigating the symmetries of a particular polyhedron. During your research, you come across a polynomial that describes the relationship between the number of vertices \( V \), edges \( E \), and faces \( F \) of the polyhedron, given by Euler's formula: \( V - E + F = 2 \).

1. Suppose the number of vertices \( V \) is given by the polynomial equation \( V = x^2 + 3x + 2 \), and the number of faces \( F \) is given by \( F = 2x + 1 \). If the number of edges \( E \) is \( 2x^2 + x + 1 \), verify Euler's formula for this polyhedron when \( x = 1 \).

2. After verifying Euler's formula, you decide to explore further by considering a transformation of the polyhedron that doubles the number of vertices, faces, and edges. Write down the new polynomial expressions for the transformed polyhedron's vertices, edges, and faces, using the original expressions, and verify if the transformed polyhedron still satisfies Euler's formula.

A policy analyst is working on a project that involves analyzing the financial impact of two different policy proposals. The first proposal involves a polynomial equation that models the cost (in millions of dollars) of implementing the policy over time, given by \( C(t) = 2t^3 - 9t^2 + 15t + 5 \), where \( t \) is the number of years after implementation. 

1. Solve the equation \( C(t) = 0 \) to determine the number of years after which the implementation cost becomes zero.

The second proposal involves a cost model based on a quadratic equation, given by \( Q(t) = -3t^2 + 12t + 20 \).

2. Determine the range of years for which the implementation cost is greater than 40 million dollars by solving the inequality \( Q(t) > 40 \).

An online personality, known for challenging the accuracy of statisticians' predictions, decides to publish their own growth prediction model for their follower count. This model is based on the assumption that their growth rate is contrary to the normal prediction trends. 

1. The personality claims that their follower count \( F(t) \) over time \( t \) (in months) follows the polynomial function:
   \[
   F(t) = -2t^3 + 15t^2 - 36t + 100
   \]
   a) Find the time \( t \) (in months) when the follower count reaches exactly 200. 

2. They also argue that the rate of change of their follower count will never drop below 10 followers per month. Verify this claim by analyzing the derivative \( F'(t) \) and finding the values of \( t \) for which the rate of change is less than 10 followers per month.

Michael Eismann, known for his overconfidence in his math skills during college, once claimed he could solve any quadratic equation faster than anyone else in the class. Challenge his claim by solving the following problem, which is inspired by a peculiar incident during a lecture that you both attended:

1. Solve the quadratic equation: \( x^2 - (3k+4)x + (2k^2 + 5k + 3) = 0 \) for all values of \( k \) such that the roots are real and distinct.

2. After solving, express the product of the roots in terms of \( k \) and find the minimum value of this product for the real and distinct roots condition.

A young patient, Alex, is diagnosed with a rare medical condition. The specialist doctor suggests a treatment plan that involves a daily medication regimen. The effectiveness of the treatment is represented by the polynomial function \( E(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 11t - 6 \), where \( E(t) \) is the effectiveness score and \( t \) is the number of weeks since the treatment started.

1. To determine when the treatment will be optimally effective, Alex needs to find the weeks \( t \) when the effectiveness score \( E(t) \) is zero. Solve the polynomial equation \( E(t) = 0 \) to find the values of \( t \).

2. The doctor also mentions that the treatment is considered successful if the effectiveness score \( E(t) \) is greater than or equal to 2. Determine the range of weeks \( t \) for which \( E(t) \geq 2 \).

Dr. Thompson, an archaeologist, has discovered a hoard of ancient British coins. After examining the collection, she identifies two distinct types of coins: Type A and Type B. She notes that the total number of coins is 100 and the total value of the coins is $4500. The value of each Type A coin is represented by the polynomial expression \(3x + 5\), and the value of each Type B coin is represented by \(2x + 10\).

1. If there are 40 Type A coins, set up and solve the equation to find the number of Type B coins and the value of \(x\).
   
2. Assuming the polynomial expressions for the value of each coin type, determine the total value of Type A and Type B coins separately, using the value of \(x\) found in the first sub-problem.

An epidemiologist is analyzing the spread of a disease in two regions, A and B. The number of cases in region A is modeled by the polynomial function \( f(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + 6x \), where \( x \) is the number of weeks since the disease started spreading. The number of cases in region B is modeled by the polynomial function \( g(x) = 2x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x + 5 \).

1. Determine the time (in weeks) when both regions have the same number of cases by solving the equation \( f(x) = g(x) \).

2. The epidemiologist is tasked with identifying the week where the infrastructure improvement should be prioritized. This is the week where the difference in the number of cases between the two regions is the greatest. Find the value of \( x \) that maximizes the absolute value of the difference \( |f(x) - g(x)| \).

Abstract:

Evaluating online continuing medical education seminars : evidence for improving clinical practices . The purpose of this study was to evaluate the potential for online continuing medical education ( CME ) seminars to improve quality of care . Primary care physicians ( 113 ) participated in a randomized controlled trial to evaluate an online CME series . Physicians were randomized to view either a seminar about type 2 diabetes or a seminar about systolic heart failure . Following the seminar , physicians were presented with 4 clinical vignettes and asked to describe what tests , treatments , counseling , or referrals they would recommend . Physicians who viewed the seminars were significantly more likely to recommend guideline-consistent care to patients in the vignettes . For example , physicians who viewed the diabetes seminar were significantly more likely to order an eye exam for diabetes patients ( 63 % ) compared with physicians in the control group ( 27 % ) . For some guidelines there were no group differences . These results provide early evidence of the effectiveness of online CME programs to improve physician clinical practice .

Abstract:

Pharmacological modulation of pain-related brain activity during normal and central sensitization states in humans. Abnormal processing of somatosensory inputs in the central nervous system (central sensitization) is the mechanism accounting for the enhanced pain sensitivity in the skin surrounding tissue injury (secondary hyperalgesia). Secondary hyperalgesia shares clinical characteristics with neurogenic hyperalgesia in patients with neuropathic pain. Abnormal brain responses to somatosensory stimuli have been found in patients with hyperalgesia as well as in normal subjects during experimental central sensitization. The aim of this study was to assess the effects of gabapentin, a drug effective in neuropathic pain patients, on brain processing of nociceptive information in normal and central sensitization states. Using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) in normal volunteers, we studied the gabapentin-induced modulation of brain activity in response to nociceptive mechanical stimulation of normal skin and capsaicin-induced secondary hyperalgesia. The dose of gabapentin was 1,800 mg per os, in a single administration. We found that (i) gabapentin reduced the activations in the bilateral operculoinsular cortex, independently of the presence of central sensitization; (ii) gabapentin reduced the activation in the brainstem, only during central sensitization; (iii) gabapentin suppressed stimulus-induced deactivations, only during central sensitization; this effect was more robust than the effect on brain activation. The observed drug-induced effects were not due to changes in the baseline fMRI signal. These findings indicate that gabapentin has a measurable antinociceptive effect and a stronger antihyperalgesic effect most evident in the brain areas undergoing deactivation, thus supporting the concept that gabapentin is more effective in modulating nociceptive transmission when central sensitization is present.

Paper text:

We propose a method for quantifying uncertainty in neural network regression models when the targets are real values on a $d$-dimensional simplex, such as probabilities.
We show that each target can be modeled as a sample from a Dirichlet distribution, where the parameters of the Dirichlet are provided by the output of a neural network, and that the combined model can be trained using the gradient of the data likelihood.
This approach provides interpretable predictions in the form of multidimensional distributions, rather than point estimates, from which one can obtain confidence intervals or quantify risk in decision making.
Furthermore, we show that the same approach can be used to model targets in the form of empirical counts as samples from the Dirichlet-multinomial compound distribution.
In experiments, we verify that our approach provides these benefits without harming the performance of the point estimate predictions on two diverse applications: (1) distilling deep convolutional networks trained on CIFAR-100, and (2) predicting the location of particle collisions in the XENON1T Dark Matter detector.
Artificial neural networks are typically trained by maximizing the conditional likelihood of output targets given input features.
Each target is modeled as a sample from a distribution p(y|x) parameterized by the output activity of the neural network, where the choice of parametric distribution is implied by the choice of objective function.
Thus, the support of the probability distribution should match the target space, but in practice, this is often not the case.Today, the vast majority of neural network output layers implicitly model the targets as samples from one of four distributions: a binomial, a categorical, a Gaussian, or a Laplacian distributionrespectively corresponding to the binomial cross-entropy loss, multi-class cross-entropy loss, mean squared error, and mean absolute error.
These distributions are commonly used even when the target space does not match the support, because the gradient calculations for these distributions are simple (and easy to compute) when paired with the appropriate output layer activation functions.
These distributions dominate to such a degree that few alternatives are even available in most common deep learning software packages such as Keras BID3 and PyTorch BID15 .Alternatives
do exist -using neural networks to parameterize more complex distributions is not new. The standard
regression approach can be generalized to a heteroskedastic Gaussian output layer BID14 BID18 , where the neural network predicts both a mean and a variance for each target. Multi-model
distributions can be modeled with a mixture density BID1 . And more recently
, the Gamma output layer was proposed to model targets in R >0 BID13 . In principle, any
parametric distribution with well-defined gradients could serve as a probabilistic prediction at the output of a neural network model.The approach proposed here is simpler than the one taken by Conditional Variational Autoencoders (CVAEs) BID10 BID16 . While CVAEs can,
in theory, model arbitrary high-dimensional conditional distributions, computing the exact conditional likelihood of a target requires marginalizing over intermediate representations, making exact gradient calculations intractable. Thus, training a
CVAE requires approximating the gradients through sampling. In this work we
show that restricting the output to a particular class of distributions, namely the Dirichlet or Dirichlet-multinomial compound distributions, enables a calculation of the exact likelihood of the targets and the exact gradients.Interpreting the output of a neural network classifier as a probability distribution has obvious benefits. One can derive
different point estimates, define confidence intervals, or integrate over possible outcomes -a necessity for managing risk in decision making. Potentially, it
could also lead to better learning -matching the output support to the target space essentially constrains the learning problem by incorporating outside knowledge. Allowing the network
to output "uninformative" distributions -e.g. a uniform distribution over the support -could make training faster by allowing the network to focus on the easiest training examples first -a self-guided form of curriculum learning.In the present work, we derive gradients for the Beta distribution, Dirichlet distribution, and Dirichlet-multinomial compound distribution. We then propose activation
functions that stabilize numerical optimization with stochastic gradient descent. Finally, we demonstrate through
experiments that this approach can be used to model three common types of targets: (1) targets over the multivariate simplex, (2) real-valued scalar targets with lower and upper bounds, and (3) nonnegative integer-valued counts (samples from the Dirichlet-multinomial compound distribution). The experiments demonstrate that
our approach provides interpretable predictions with learned uncertainty, without decreasing the performance of the point estimates.
In most artificial neural network models, supervised learning corresponds to maximizing the NLL of the training set targets conditioned on the inputs.
In this interpretation, each neural network prediction is a distribution over possible target values.
While the vast majority of neural network classifiers in use today rely on a small set of distributions -the binomial distribution, the categorical distribution, the Gaussian distribution, or the Laplacian distribution -there are many situations for which none of these distributions are appropriate.

We show that a neural network can parameterize these distributions and the entire model can be trained using gradient descent on the NLL of the training data targets.This provides a particularly elegant approach to modelling certain types of network targets.
The Beta and Dirichlet provide a better way to model targets that lie on a simplex, such as probabilities or realvalues that lie on a bounded interval, and the Dirichlet-multinomial enables us to model vectors of counts using the elegant mathematical properties of the Dirichlet.
The predicted distributions have the correct support, so we can use them in decision making and for confidence intervals.
